steps.title: Test the texture
steps.body: Grab a damp handful of soil and squeeze it. Sandy soil falls apart, clay stays in a tight ball, and loam forms a loose crumb.

steps.title: Jar test for composition
steps.body: Fill a jar one-third with soil, top with water, shake, and let it settle overnight. Sand, silt and clay separate into visible bands.
checklist: Fill jar with soil and water

steps.title: Check the pH
steps.body: Most vegetables prefer pH 6.0-7.0. Test with a kit and record the reading before amending.

steps.title: Pick a spot
steps.body: Choose a level, well-drained spot out of direct wind, ideally part-shade.
checklist: Easy to reach with a wheelbarrow

steps.title: Layer browns and greens
steps.body: Build in alternating layers, roughly two parts browns to one part greens by volume.
checklist: Add greens in a thin layer

steps.title: Add water and turn
steps.body: The pile should be as damp as a wrung-out sponge. Turn it every one to two weeks.

steps.title: Remove suckers
steps.body: Pinch out the small shoots that grow in the angle between the main stem and a leaf branch.

steps.title: Trim lower leaves
steps.body: Remove leaves touching the soil to reduce splash-borne disease.

steps.title: Take the cutting
steps.body: Cut a 10-15cm stem just below a leaf node, then remove the lower leaves.

steps.title: Pot and cover
steps.body: Dip the base in rooting hormone, push into moist compost, and cover with a clear bag.

steps.title: Keep moist and warm
steps.body: Place in bright, indirect light and keep compost moist until roots form.

steps.title: Inspect undersides
steps.body: Aphids, whitefly and mites hide under leaves. Check a few leaves per plant, top and bottom.

steps.title: Identify before acting
steps.body: Not every insect is a pest. Note what you find and confirm before spraying anything.

steps.title: Clear spent plants
steps.body: Remove finished annuals and diseased material, but leave healthy seed heads for wildlife.

steps.title: Mulch bare soil
steps.body: Cover bare beds with a 5-8cm layer of mulch to protect soil structure over winter.
